summary: The residual is 280 pixels, every one exactly -1 on R,G,B with alpha identical (two 10x7 blocks in a 900x900 frame). Ruffle's copy_pixels_with_alpha_source deliberately does NOT use its FLASH_PREMUL_FACTOR table here: it un-premultiplies with f64 division and .round(), then re-premultiplies with (c*a+127)/255. We call unpremultiplyAlpha(), which IS the table. Every other step in the arm already matches Ruffle exactly ((ab_alpha*sa)>>8, premultiplyAlpha, blend_over's truncating /255). summary: 'Device-font glyph placement under a matrix' is wrong: extra_ink ~= 0 and shift_gain = 0.00 on all five rows, missing_ink 0.156-1.000 — our ink is a strict SUBSET of Ruffle's, i.e. absent glyphs, not displaced ones. In edittext_device_transform_basic the embedded-font column is pixel-identical and every differing pixel is in the device-font column (same TTF). Root cause: the recompiler's device-font importer emits metrics only (codes/advances/kern/ascent/descent), the runtime Noto fallback is metrics-only by construction, and ng_find_device_fallback_font only works when the SWF itself declares a synthesized _sans. So device text has correct metrics (its trace rows pass) and no outlines. Ruffle builds device glyphs exactly like embedded ones, so exact pixel agreement is achievable — the embedded column proves our rasteriser matches when the outlines match. Traps: NonZero fill rule for TTF contours; cubics only for CFF/embedAsCFF; the emitted glyph rows must be visible to both the AVM1 and AVM2 text paths.
risk: medium-high — four of five rows are tolerance 0 with tiny outlier budgets; leading_device_font (tolerance 128) is the one row coverage alone can flip
